long_biography.plain_text:
Palais Vénitien began with an extravagant architectural idea: a Renaissance-inspired residence overlooking Cannes. Adil Khashoggi bought the hillside land in the late 1980s and started construction, but a planning dispute left the shell unfinished for years. His son Emad eventually revived and completed it.

Long before the French project, Khashoggi had entered international business through Triad alongside his older brothers, Adnan and Essam. The Berkeley graduate participated in a group whose interests stretched across industry, finance and property, although Adnan held nearly all of its parent-company equity. Adil later carved out his own path in real estate, directing developments in Saudi Arabia and taking interests in European property companies. By the mid-2010s, he was retired.
